title: B1-13 · The numerals: cardinals, ordinals, dates

blocks.text: B1-13 · The numerals: cardinals, ordinals, dates
Lesson overview

Arabic numerals are famous for their difficulty: the genre is opposite from 3 a 10, the singular or plural name changing by digit, cases. In newspapers, numbers are almost always written in figures, but those who read aloud a news bulletin, those who say a date or those who translate a document need to know how they say. In this unit you put together the whole system, from units to millions, order them, fractions, dates in the two calendars and hours. Two weeks.

rows: 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 120–121), plus the EGY track

blocks.text: Materials This unit, Grammar G53, script for speech synthesis, session with tutor
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. Numbers 1–10 with the name (inverse genre from 3 a 10, plural genitive);
2. use numbers 11–99 with the singular accusative name, including 11 and 12;
3. use hundreds, thousands and millions under the singular name of genitive;
4. Form and grant of orders ( ⁧الأَوَّل⁩ , ⁧الحَادِي عَشَرَ⁩ , ⁧الحَادِي وَالعِشْرُونَ⁩ );
5. to say fractions and percentages, dates (gregorian calendar and Egira), centuries, decades and hours;
6. read out figures and give them in a chronicle text.
Two-week plan.

blocks.text: 1. Dialogue 1 · Registration to the institute
Luca calls the Cairo Institute to complete his membership.

rows: The clerk: Institute of Languages, good morning.
⁧صَبَاحَ النُّورِ. اِسْمِي لُوكَا، سَجَّلْتُ فِي الدَّوْرَةِ الصَّيْفِيَّةِ، وَأُرِيدُ أَنْ⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ ⁧أَتَأَكَّدَ مِنْ بَعْضِ التَّفَاصِيلِ.⁩
Good morning. My name is Luca, I signed up for the summer class and I'd like to check out some details.
⁧نَعَمْ، وَجَدْتُهُ. تَبْدَأُ الدَّوْرَةُ يَوْمَ السَّادِسِ مِنْ يُولْيُو، وَتَسْتَمِرُّ⁩ : ⁧المُوَظَّفَة⁩ ⁧أَرْبَعَةَ أَسَابِيعَ.⁩
The employee: Yes, I found him. The course begins on 6 July and lasts four weeks.
And how many hours a week?
⁧عِشْرُونَ سَاعَةً: أَرْبَعُ سَاعَاتٍ يَوْمِيًّا، مِنَ الأَحَدِ إِلَى الخَمِيسِ.⁩ : ⁧المُوَظَّفَة⁩ ⁧وَهُنَاكَ أَيْضًا ثَلَاثُ رِحْلَاتٍ ثَقَافِيَّةٍ.⁩
The employee: Twenty hours: four hours a day, from Sunday to Thursday. There are also three cultural trips.
⁧سَبْعُمِئَةٍ وَخَمْسُونَ دُولَارًا، دَفَعْتَ مِنْهَا ثُلُثَهَا، أَيْ مِئَتَيْنِ⁩ : ⁧المُوَظَّفَة⁩ ⁧وَخَمْسِينَ. يَبْقَى خَمْسُمِئَةِ دُولَارٍ تَدْفَعُهَا فِي اليَوْمِ الأَوَّلِ.⁩
The employee: $700, $50, of which you paid a third, that is, $250. Five hundred dollars left to pay on the first day.
Luca: And in what class are they?
⁧فِي المُسْتَوَى الرَّابِعِ، القَاعَةُ رَقْمُ اثْنَيْ عَشَرَ، فِي الطَّابِقِ⁩ : ⁧المُوَظَّفَة⁩ ⁧الثَّالِثِ. وَعَدَدُ الطُّلَّابِ فِي الصَّفِّ أَحَدَ عَشَرَ طَالِبًا وَطَالِبَةً.⁩
The employee: On the fourth level, room number twelve, on the third floor. The students in the class are eleven, between boys and girls.
⁧شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا. إِلَى اللِّقَاءِ فِي السَّادِسِ مِنْ يُولْيُو!⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩
Thank you very much. Goodbye to the 6 July!

blocks.text: What to notice. ⁧أَرْبَعَةَ أَسَابِيعَ⁩ 4 weeks (0 to 0): 3–10 with the plural genitive, the male number because ⁧أُسْبُوع⁩ It's male. ⁧أَرْبَعُ سَاعَاتٍ⁩ , ⁧ثَلَاثُ رِحْلَاتٍ⁩ : number without ⁧ة⁩ because the name is female. ⁧عِشْرُونَ سَاعَةً⁩ , ⁧أَحَدَ عَشَرَ طَالِبًا⁩ : 11–99 with the singular accusative. ⁧سَبْعُمِئَةٍ وَخَمْسُونَ دُولَارًا⁩ : the last element (50) decides the form of the name. ⁧خَمْسُمِئَةِ دُولَارٍ⁩ : 100 and multiples with the singular genitive. ⁧السَّادِسِ مِنْ يُولْيُو⁩ , ⁧المُسْتَوَى الرَّابِعِ⁩ , ⁧الطَّابِقِ الثَّالِثِ⁩ , ⁧اليَوْمِ الأَوَّلِ⁩ : order them. ⁧ثُلُثَهَا⁩ A third of them. ⁧القَاعَةُ رَقْمُ اثْنَيْ عَشَرَ⁩ : after ⁧رَقْم⁩ The number goes to the genitive. ⁧التَّفَاصِيل⁩ The details are given. ⁧الرُّسُوم⁩ The fee, the taxes. ⁧أَيْ⁩ • i.e.
2. The overall picture

rows: singular, dual (the number follows as adjective)

blocks.text: In the composite numbers, the last element pronounced shall be decided: ⁧مِئَةٌ وَعِشْرُونَ طَالِبًا⁩ ( 20 → singular accusation), ⁧أَلْفٌ وَثَلَاثَةُ طُلَّابٍ⁩ ( 3 → plural genitive).
3. From 1 a 10

1 and 2 they go after the name, as adjectives, and usually just to insist: ⁧عِنْدِي سُؤَالٌ وَاحِدٌ⁩ I only have one question. The name is normally sufficient ( ⁧سُؤَالٌ⁩ ) or the dual ( ⁧سُؤَالَانِ⁩ ). 3–10: the reverse genre. The number takes the ⁧ة⁩ if the singular of the name is male, do not take it if it is female:
⁧طَالِبَة⁩ f. ⁧سَبْعُ طَالِبَاتٍ⁩ seven students

Attention: it counts the kind of singular, not plural. ⁧رِجَال⁩ Is it a plural that looks feminine? No: the singular ⁧رَجُل⁩ is male → ⁧خَمْسَةُ رِجَالٍ⁩ . ⁧سِجِلَّات⁩ has the shape in ⁧ـات⁩ but the singular ⁧سِجِلّ⁩ is male → ⁧ثَلَاثَةُ⁩

The case of the number depends on its function in the sentence: ⁧وَصَلَ ثَلَاثَةُ طُلَّابٍ⁩ (subject), ⁧رَأَيْتُ ثَلَاثَةَ طُلَّابٍ⁩ (object), ⁧مَعَ ثَلَاثَةِ طُلَّابٍ⁩ (after preposition). ⁧ثَمَانٍ⁩ * 8" (feminine) behaves like defects: ⁧ثَمَانِي سَاعَاتٍ⁩ in iḍāfa.
4. From 11 a 99
11 and 12
12 (a.c. · Jan.) ⁧اثْنَتَيْ عَشْرَةَ طَالِبَةًاثْنَيْ عَشَرَ طَالِبًا⁩
13–19: Unity follows the reverse genre, ⁧عَشَر⁩ / ⁧عَشْرَة⁩ follows the name genre; Both sides are invariant with the fatha.
⁧خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ يَوْمًا⁩ 15 days

20–90: forms in ⁧ـُونَ⁩ / ⁧ـِينَ⁩ ( ⁧عِشْرُونَ⁩ , ⁧ثَلَاثُونَ⁩ … ⁧تِسْعُونَ⁩ ), the same for male and female, who decline as healthy plurals: ⁧عِشْرُونَ⁩ (No.), ⁧عِشْرِينَ⁩ (Ac., Jan.). 21–99: First the unit, then the ten, joined by ⁧وَ⁩ ; the unit follows the rules of 1–10 (1 and 2 granted, 3–9 Inverse genre): ⁧وَاحِدٌ وَعِشْرُونَ طَالِبًا⁩ , ⁧إِحْدَى وَعِشْرُونَ طَالِبَةً⁩ , ⁧ثَلَاثَةٌ وَثَلَاثُونَ يَوْمًا⁩ , ⁧ثَلَاثٌ وَثَلَاثُونَ سَنَةً⁩ . Both sides decline.
5. Hundreds, thousands, millions

The order of the big numbers. In the modern language we read from the greatest to the smallest: ⁧١٩٨٧⁩ = ⁧أَلْفٌ وَتِسْعُمِئَةٍ وَسَبْعَةٌ وَثَمَانُونَ⁩ . The classical form, from the smallest to the largest ( ⁧سَبْعَةٌ وَثَمَانُونَ وَتِسْعُمِئَةٍ وَأَلْفٌ⁩ ), is found in formal and religious texts: recognize it. The name after a large number follows the last element: ⁧أَلْفٌ وَخَمْسُمِئَةِ طَالِبٍ⁩ ( 500 → genitive), ⁧أَلْفَانِ وَعِشْرُونَ طَالِبًا⁩ ( 20 → accusative). Practical reading. Many speakers simplify the endings when reading the news aloud; You look for at least the right gender and the right form of the name.
6. Dialogue 2 · Family dates
Hudā Show Luca the family photos on the phone.
⁧اُنْظُرْ، هٰذَا آدَمُ. أَتَمَّ أَمْسِ شَهْرَهُ السَّابِعَ!⁩ : ⁧هُدَى⁩ Hudā: Look, this is Ādam. Yesterday he turned seven months!

rows: ⁧مَا شَاءَ اللهُ! وُلِدَ فِي الصَّيْفِ، صَحِيحٌ؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩
Luca: That's nice! He was born in the summer, wasn't he?

⁧، كَمَا⁩ « ⁧جْوِيلِيَة⁩ » ⁧أَوْ⁩ … ⁧نَعَمْ، فِي الخَامِسِ وَالعِشْرِينَ مِنْ يُولْيُو⁩ : ⁧هُدَى⁩ ⁧يَقُولُ أَبِي! وَهٰذِهِ جَدَّتِي: سَتَحْتَفِلُ بِعِيدِ مِيلَادِهَا الخَامِسِ وَالثَّمَانِينَ⁩ ⁧فِي الشَّهْرِ القَادِمِ.⁩
Hudā: Yes, on July 25 ... or "juwiliya" , as my father says! And this is my grandmother: next month she celebrates her 85th birthday.
Eighty-five years! And where does he live?

⁧فِي صَفَاقِسَ، فِي تُونِسَ. أَبِي جَاءَ إِلَى إِيطَالِيَا وَحْدَهُ فِي أَوَاخِرِ⁩ : ⁧هُدَى⁩ ⁧الثَّمَانِينِيَّاتِ، سَنَةَ أَلْفٍ وَتِسْعِمِئَةٍ وَتِسْعٍ وَثَمَانِينَ، وَتَعَرَّفَ إِلَى أُمِّي بَعْدَ⁩ ⁧سَنَتَيْنِ.⁩
Hudā: In Sfax, Tunisia. My father came to Italy alone at the end of the 1980s, in 1989And she met my mom two years later.
And how many grandchildren does your grandmother have?
⁧وَخَمْسَةُ أَحْفَادِ أَحْفَادٍ، وَآدَمُ⁩ … ⁧ثَلَاثَةَ عَشَرَ حَفِيدًا وَحَفِيدَةً⁩ : ⁧هُدَى⁩ ⁧أَصْغَرُهُمْ!⁩
Hudā: Thirteen grandchildren and five great-grandchildren, and Ādam He's the youngest!
⁧عَائِلَةٌ كَبِيرَةٌ! فِي عَائِلَتِي نَحْنُ سِتَّةُ أَشْخَاصٍ فَقَط.⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩
A big family! Mine's only six people.

blocks.text: ⁧سِتَّةٌ؟ هٰذَا عَدَدُ أَبْنَاءِ عَمِّي وَحْدَهُمْ!⁩ : ⁧هُدَى⁩ Hudā: Six? There are as many as my uncle's only children!

What to notice. ⁧شَهْرَهُ السَّابِعَ⁩ Its seventh month is: ordinal. ⁧الخَامِسِ وَالعِشْرِينَ مِنْ يُولْيُو⁩ On 25 July: Date by order (section) 8). ⁧جْوِيلِيَة⁩ : the Tunisian name of July, from French (section 8). ⁧عِيدِ مِيلَادِهَا الخَامِسِ وَالثَّمَانِينَ⁩ It's his 85or birthday •: composed order. ⁧خَمْسٌ وَثَمَانُونَ سَنَةً⁩ : 85 with ⁧سَنَة⁩ ( f.) → ⁧خَمْسٌ⁩ without ⁧ة. فِي أَوَاخِرِ الثَّمَانِينِيَّاتِ⁩ At the end of the 1980s. ⁧سَنَةَ أَلْفٍ وَتِسْعِمِئَةٍ وَتِسْعٍ وَثَمَانِينَ⁩ : 1989 read by the largest; ⁧تِسْعٍ⁩ without ⁧ة⁩ why ⁧سَنَة⁩ It's feminine. ⁧ثَلَاثَةَ عَشَرَ حَفِيدًا⁩ : 13 with a male name. ⁧سِتَّةُ أَشْخَاصٍ. أَتَمَّ⁩ It's done. ⁧حَفِيد⁩ "Grandpa's grandson," pl. ⁧أَحْفَاد. صَفَاقِس⁩ Sfax, diptototo (B1-14).
7. Order them

The ordinals are adjectives: they go after the name and generally agree, case and determination: ⁧الدَّرْسُ الثَّالِثُ⁩ , ⁧فِي الطَّبْعَةِ الثَّانِيَةِ⁩ . Exception ⁧أَوَّل⁩ , which is also used in front of the name in iḍāfa: ⁧أَوَّلُ مَرَّةٍ⁩ The first time that the product has been manufactured, ⁧أَوَّلُ امْرَأَةٍ⁩ The first woman to be married. The ordinal adverbs: ⁧أَوَّلًا⁩ , ⁧ثَانِيًا⁩ , ⁧ثَالِثًا⁩ . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ⁧أَخِيرًا⁩ Finally, it is. The only modern language uses for the ordinals over the ten also the form with ⁧رَقْم⁩ : ⁧الدَّرْسُ رَقْمُ خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ⁩ • Lesson No. 15 •
8. Fractions, percentages, dates and hours

Fractions. ⁧نِصْف⁩ «½», ⁧ثُلُث⁩ «⅓», ⁧رُبْع⁩ «¼», ⁧خُمْس⁩ «⅕», ⁧سُدْس⁩ , ⁧سُبْع⁩ , ⁧ثُمْن⁩ , ⁧تُسْع⁩ , ⁧عُشْر⁩ The following table is added: ⁧فُعْل⁩ ); plural ⁧أَثْلَاث⁩ , ⁧أَرْبَاع⁩ : ⁧ثَلَاثَةُ أَرْبَاعٍ⁩ “three quarters”. With a name: ⁧ثُلُثُ السُّكَّانِ⁩ One third of the inhabitants of the country. Percentages. ⁧خَمْسَةٌ وَعِشْرُونَ بِالمِئَةِ⁩ / ⁧فِي المِئَةِ⁩ « 25%»; ⁧نِسْبَةُ خَمْسَةٍ وَعِشْرِينَ بِالمِئَةِ⁩ . The symbol in the texts: ⁧٪⁩ o %. Dates.

rows: in the seventies · in the eighties of the last century

blocks.text: The day of the month is said by the ordinal: ⁧الأَوَّلُ مِنْ مَايُو⁩ On 1 May the following shall be added: ⁧العِشْرُونَ مِنْ يُونْيُو⁩ On 20 June. In the documents and newspapers there is also the cardinal written in figures: ⁧٦ يُولْيُو.⁩ The months have two sets of names: the international one (Egypt, Maghreb, Gulf) and the Syriac one (Levant and Iraq).

In the pan-Arab newspapers, both are often found: ⁧٦ يُولْيُو⁩ ( ⁧تَمُّوز⁩ ). In the Maghreb there are other series: in Tunisia and Algeria names taken from French ( ⁧جَانْفِي⁩ January 2019 ⁧جْوِيلِيَة⁩ July 2015 ⁧أُوت⁩ In Morocco forms ⁧يُولْيُوز⁩ July 2015 ⁧غُشْت⁩ August. Just recognize them. The hours use the female ordinals (successed ⁧السَّاعَة⁩ ): ⁧السَّاعَةُ الثَّالِثَةُ⁩ The following points are added: ⁧الثَّالِثَةُ وَالرُّبْعُ⁩ • the three and a quarter of them; ⁧الرَّابِعَةُ إِلَّا رُبْعًا⁩ • the four minus a quarter • ⁧الحَادِيَةَ عَشْرَةَ وَالنِّصْفُ⁩ • 11:30.
9. Pronunciation

Long shapes. ṯalāṯata ʿašara, iṯnatā ʿašrata, al-ḥādiya ʿašrata: practice reading them in one breath. Read the figures. The tutor writes ten numbers in oriental Arabic digits ( ⁧٣٤٧⁩ , ⁧١٩٨٩⁩ , ⁧٢٠٢٦⁩ …); You read them by the name that follows. Remember: the figures are also read from left to right in an Arabic text.
10. New lexicon

rows: ⁧بِمُعَدَّلِ⁩ On average, at the rate of

blocks.text: ★ ⁧أَوَاخِر⁩ awāḫir the end (of a period) ⁧أ خ ر⁩ plural name ⁧فِي أَوَاخِرِ⁩ At the end of this section ⁧فِي أَوَائِلِ⁩ At the beginning of this section:

Notes of use. ⁧عَقْد⁩ means either ... or contract...: ⁧فِي العَقْدِ الأَخِيرِ⁩ In the last decade, ⁧عَقْدُ عَمَلٍ⁩ The contract of employment is defined as "work contract." ⁧بِمُعَدَّلِ⁩ is useful for the averages: ⁧بِمُعَدَّلِ ثَلَاثِ سَاعَاتٍ يَوْمِيًّا⁩ On average, three hours a day is the same. ⁧حَوَالَيْ⁩ is followed by the genitive: ⁧حَوَالَيْ أَلْفِ شَخْصٍ.⁩
